theorem_title: A supplied Egyptian-fraction representation has a least possible length
natural_language_statement:
Let $L,t\in\mathbb N$. Suppose there is a list of exactly $t$ distinct positive natural numbers, each at least $L$, whose reciprocals sum to 1. Then there exists a natural number $m$ such that

$$
\exists\, d_1,\ldots,d_m\text{ distinct},\quad d_i>0,\quad d_i\geq L,\quad\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac1{d_i}=1,\qquad m\leq u\ \text{for every such representation of length }u.
$$

This is a well-ordering consequence for the set of attainable lengths. Existence of one representation is a required premise, including when the lower bound is zero; positivity of every denominator remains required.
